disputable.why: Some players won't count a Roman numeral as a word; the Rule's space-separated definition keeps him in.

wording.why: Wukong's alternate name 'Monkey King' is two words; a player typing it may expect credit, but the official name is one word.
wording.suggestion: Add to the Rule: 'Wukong counts as one word, even though he's also called the Monkey King.'

wording.why: Players may treat apostrophes (Kai'Sa, Cho'Gath) or the ampersand as word breaks; the Rule only says spaces and only covers Nunu & Willump.
wording.suggestion: Words are separated by spaces in the champion's official name: Dr. Mundo and Jarvan IV are two words; Kai'Sa is one; Nunu & Willump is three.

aliases.why: Players type the numeral as a digit.

fun.why: Only 10 answers and the famous ones (Lee Sin, Master Yi, MF, TF) come instantly; veterans can name nearly all, so the rare end is thin.

champion:LeeSin.why: First two-word name most players reach for.

champion:MissFortune.why: Famous; MF reminds players it's two words.

champion:XinZhao.why: Well known, full name used often.

champion:DrMundo.why: Players debate whether 'Dr.' counts, which slows them.

champion:AurelionSol.why: Often just 'ASol'; full name less front-of-mind.

champion:JarvanIV.why: Usually 'J4'; numeral as a word is easy to overlook.

champion:Renata.why: Most players only know 'Renata'; few recall the surname Glasc.

gemCandidates.why: Maintainer's suggestion holds: she's known as 'Renata', so 'Renata Glasc' is an 'oh, right, she has a surname' reveal. Typicality 0.1, bottom of the set.
Everyone knows him but says 'Tahm'; a satisfying full-name reveal at 0.18, bottom half.
'IV is a word!' is a fun reveal at 0.2; ranked third because some players dispute numerals as words.
